text:
Ava (People Ops): Thanks everyone who joined the all-hands — following up with a live Q&A on remote/hybrid + office ops. Drop questions here and we'll answer live / compile into the FAQ. :wave:
Maya (Eng): Quick one — what counts as 'company-sponsored travel' vs. personal travel for offsites? Reimbursements?
Riley (Finance): Company-sponsored = events that are on the official calendar and approved by a manager. Use expense code `OFFSITE-TRVL` and attach the approval email. Personal add-ons (upgrades, extra nights) are out-of-pocket unless pre-approved.
Sam (Office Ops): For logistics, we'll publish a suggested travel window and shared hotel link for each offsite. If you want a room upgrade, ping me 2 weeks prior and we'll check budget.
Ava (People Ops): On the WFH/hybrid policy — core days are Tue/Thu for cross-team sync; managers can set team-specific expectations beyond that. No one will be forced into a daily onsite schedule unless it's role-critical.
Maya (Eng): Are we making any changes to the workspace stipend? Mine barely covered a monitor last year.
Ava (People Ops): Stipend remains $750/year for home workspace; new option: one-time large purchase (desk/ergonomic chair) reimbursed up to $500 if submitted with a short justification. You can still use the full stipend for smaller items.
Elliot (CEO): Short note from leadership — we want flexibility, but also predictable overlap for collaboration. If a team needs 3 in-office days for a quarter bug bash or onboarding, that's fine with notice. We'll keep the default lightweight.
Maya (Eng): Thanks — on travel approvals, is manager + finance required or is manager ok alone?
Riley (Finance): Manager approval is required first; Finance will auto-approve routine offsites under $5k per person. Anything above goes to leadership review.
Sam (Office Ops): For local office desks: hot-desking is still in place at HQ — use the desk-reservation tool. We have a handful of long-term desks for accommodation requests; submit via the form and we'll review.
Ava (People Ops): Clarifying return-to-office reimbursements: commute < 50 miles no reimbursement; if your role is moved and you must commute > 60 miles temporarily for a business need, we can discuss a housing/commute stipend case-by-case.
Maya (Eng): How do we handle international employees attending US offsites — visas and travel windows?
Riley (Finance): Company covers visa fees and standard economy travel. If you need expedited processing or premium flights, get manager sign-off before booking.
Elliot (CEO): We'll also publish a simple checklist for offsite organizers (travel approval, budget, accessibility needs, points of contact). People Ops + Office Ops will maintain it.
Ava (People Ops): We'll update the policy doc today with these clarifications. Link will be in #people-ops and the all-hands notes. If you want an exception for a specific case, DM me.
AllHandsBot: Document updated: https://internal.redwood.com/policies/remote-hybrid-2025 — summary appended to all-hands notes. :white_check_mark:
Maya (Eng): Awesome, thanks! :thumbsup:
Sam (Office Ops): Heads-up — booking window for Q3 offsite opens next Monday. More details in calendar invite.
